failureModes.prompt: When the model is confidently wrong, what should the person see?
failureModes.why: the failure looks identical to success, so nothing catches it by itself

options.label: Show it with a way to correct it
Show it plainly
options.consequence: cleanest, and wrong answers read as fact

failureModes.recommended: Show it with a way to correct it
failureModes.provenBy: a test that forces a wrong model answer and asserts the correction path is present

failureModes.prompt: If the provider is slow or unavailable, should we wait, use something simpler, or say it is unavailable?
failureModes.why: this dependency fails more often than the rest of the app

options.label: Fall back to something simpler
options.consequence: keeps the feature alive, two behaviours to maintain

failureModes.provenBy: a test that times out the provider and asserts the chosen behaviour (unavailable message, or fallback)

failureModes.prompt: Is there a point where this becomes too expensive to keep serving one person?
failureModes.why: cost scales with use here, unlike the rest of the product

options.label: Cap it per person
options.consequence: predictable spend, heavy users hit a wall

options.label: No cap for now
options.consequence: nothing interrupts anyone, spend is open-ended

failureModes.provenBy: a test that exceeds the per-person cap and asserts requests are limited as decided

failureModes.prompt: May what people write or say be sent to an outside provider?
failureModes.why: it decides what we can promise about private content

options.label: Yes, and say so plainly
options.consequence: full capability, needs a clear statement

options.label: Only with permission
options.consequence: safer promise, fewer people get the feature

failureModes.provenBy: a check that the disclosure is shown before any content leaves the device, and a test that opting out keeps content local
